identification.summary: China-based cyber-espionage actor that Microsoft tracks as Purple Typhoon (formerly POTASSIUM), mapped to APT10, menuPass, Stone Panda and Red Apollo [S1]. US prosecutors allege APT10 intrusions from about 2006 through 2018 aimed at intellectual property and confidential business information, including against managed service providers (MSPs), more than 45 technology companies and US government agencies [S2]. The group is best known for Operation Cloud Hopper, a sustained campaign against global MSPs and their clients [S4][S3], and has repeatedly targeted Japanese organizations [S5][S6][S7].
identification.firstObserved: DOJ indictment alleges activity from about 2006 [S2]; FireEye stated it had tracked APT10 since 2009 [S6]; Unit 42 reported Japanese targeting since at least 2014 [S5].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Purple Typhoon (formerly POTASSIUM); Microsoft's mapping lists POTASSIUM, STONE PANDA, GOLEM, Evilgrab, AEON, LIVESAFE, ChChes, APT10, Haymaker, Webmonder, Foxtrot, Foxmail, MenuPass and Red Apollo [S1]. Symantec tracks the actor as Cicada [S7][S8]. Several mapped names (ChChes, Evilgrab, Haymaker) are malware family names rather than vendor cluster names [S1][S5]. MirrorFace / Earth Kasha is assessed by Japan's NPA as a sub-group within the APT10 umbrella [S9]; it is kept as a related cluster here, not merged.

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China, Ministry of State Security (MSS). The December 2018 DOJ indictment alleges that two APT10 members, Zhu Hua and Zhang Shilong, worked for Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Company in Tianjin and acted in association with the MSS Tianjin State Security Bureau [S2].
attribution.confidence: UK NCSC assessed 'with the highest level of probability' that APT10 was responsible for the MSP campaign and that it is 'highly likely' APT10 has an enduring relationship with the MSS and operates to meet Chinese State requirements [S3]. The US indicted two alleged members [S2], and Canada, Australia, New Zealand and the UK also publicly attributed the activity to the MSS [S10]. Japan's NPA assesses MirrorFace as an APT10 sub-group [S9].
attribution.basis: DOJ indictment (SDNY, December 2018) [S2]; coordinated UK and allied government attribution [S3][S10]; vendor reporting from PwC/BAE (Cloud Hopper) [S4], Palo Alto Unit 42 [S5], FireEye [S6] and Symantec [S7][S8].

objectives: Theft of intellectual property and confidential business information [S2], achieved at scale by compromising MSPs that hold direct access to client networks [S4][S3]. Later campaigns collected information from government, legal, religious and NGO organizations [S8]; the MirrorFace sub-group is assessed to target Japanese national-security and advanced-technology information [S9].

sectors: Managed IT service providers (MSPs) and their clients [S3][S4]
regions: Global; MSP campaign reached providers in at least 14 countries [S4]
United States (at least a dozen states) [S2]
Japan and Japanese subsidiaries in as many as 17 regions [S7][S5][S6]
Europe, Asia and North America (2021-2022 campaign) [S8]
targeting.notes: Japan is a persistent focus across vendor reporting [S5][S6][S7]. MSP compromise expanded the scale and scope of targeting across multiple sectors [S4].

capabilities.summary: Spear-phishing with malicious, sometimes password-protected Word documents carrying VBA macros [S6]; custom and shared malware including PlugX and Poison Ivy [S4][S5], ChChes signed with a certificate leaked from HackingTeam [S5], UPPERCUT/ANEL with per-C2 encryption keys and anti-analysis changes [S6], and Backdoor.Hartip [S7]. Exploitation of the Zerologon vulnerability (2019-2020) [S7] and of Microsoft Exchange servers for initial access [S8]. DLL side-loading through a legitimate VLC Media Player and remote control with WinVNC [S8]. Abuse of trusted MSP access to pivot into client networks [S4][S3]. The MirrorFace sub-group used a revived ANEL backdoor, a customized AsyncRAT run inside Windows Sandbox, and VS Code remote tunnels [S11].

campaigns.name: menuPass targeting of Japanese academics (ChChes)
campaigns.summary: From September to November 2016 menuPass targeted Japanese academics, a Japanese pharmaceutical firm and a US subsidiary of a Japanese manufacturer, using PlugX, Poison Ivy and the new ChChes Trojan.

campaigns.name: Operation Cloud Hopper
campaigns.summary: PwC UK and BAE Systems reported sustained global campaigns against MSPs and their clients, assessed as almost certainly APT10, working with the UK NCSC to notify victims.

campaigns.name: Japanese media sector spear-phishing (UPPERCUT)
campaigns.summary: FireEye detected and blocked suspected APT10 spear-phishing against the Japanese media sector delivering an updated UPPERCUT (ANEL) backdoor.

campaigns.name: US indictment and allied attribution
campaigns.summary: DOJ charged Zhu Hua and Zhang Shilong; the UK and allies attributed the Cloud Hopper MSP campaign to APT10 acting for the MSS.

campaigns.name: Japan-linked companies campaign (Zerologon)
campaigns.summary: Symantec reported a campaign from mid-October 2019 to October 2020 against Japanese companies and subsidiaries in up to 17 regions, exploiting Zerologon.

campaigns.name: Cicada VLC side-loading campaign
campaigns.summary: From mid-2021 to at least February 2022, Cicada targeted government, legal, religious and NGO organizations in Europe, Asia and North America via Exchange access and VLC DLL side-loading.

campaigns.name: Operation AkaiRyu (MirrorFace sub-group)
campaigns.summary: ESET reported (March 2025) activity tracked in Q2-Q3 2024 of MirrorFace targeting a Central European diplomatic institute with an Expo 2025 lure and a revived ANEL backdoor; its first known European target.

campaigns.name: Japan NPA attribution of MirrorFace
campaigns.summary: Japan's NPA and NISC attributed about 210 attacks since 2019 on Japanese government agencies and companies to MirrorFace, assessed as an APT10 sub-group.

diamond.adversary: MSS-linked operators; two alleged members (Zhu Hua, Zhang Shilong) employed by Huaying Haitai in Tianjin, associated with the Tianjin State Security Bureau [S2][S3].
diamond.capability: Spear-phishing documents, PlugX, Poison Ivy, ChChes, UPPERCUT/ANEL, Hartip; Zerologon and Exchange exploitation; DLL side-loading [S4][S5][S6][S7][S8].
diamond.infrastructure: Actor-registered C2 domains overlapping with older menuPass infrastructure [S5]; compromised MSP networks used as pivots into clients [S4]; VS Code remote tunnels (MirrorFace) [S11].
diamond.victim: MSPs and their clients, technology firms, US government agencies, Japanese companies and academics, governments, NGOs, religious and legal organizations [S2][S4][S5][S7][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Intellectual-property and business-information theft serving Chinese State requirements [S2][S3]; Japanese national-security and technology information (MirrorFace) [S9].
diamond.technology: Trusted remote-administration relationships between MSPs and customers [S4]; unpatched domain controllers and Exchange servers [S7][S8].

gaps: Primary DOJ indictment text and gov.uk statement were seen only in search results and summaries, not opened; quoted wording comes from search-result excerpts [S2][S3].
Microsoft has published little public reporting under the Purple Typhoon name; this profile relies on Microsoft's naming mapping plus other vendors' reporting [S1].

Cluster boundaries: Trend Micro describes APT10 as an umbrella with Earth Kasha (LODEINFO, NOOPDOOR) and Earth Tengshe (SigLoader, SodaMaster) sub-clusters; MirrorFace/Earth Kasha's relation to Purple Typhoon in Microsoft's taxonomy is not stated in the sources gathered. Trend Micro's original reports were not retrieved.
Start date of Cloud Hopper differs: UK NCSC says since at least 2016, while other reporting cites 2014 [S3].

Symantec's original 2020 and 2022 Cicada blogs, the ESET AkaiRyu blog and the Japanese NPA report could not be fetched (host resolution errors); details come from coverage and vendor press releases [S7][S8][S9][S11].
Activity attributed specifically to Purple Typhoon after 2022 (outside the MirrorFace sub-group) is not documented in the sources gathered.

Imported record aliases ATK41, TA429, HOGFISH, Granite Taurus, BRONZE RIVERSIDE, CVNX, Cicada and Cloud Hopper were not all verified against the cited sources; only names stated by cited sources were added.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key cyber terrain includes MSP and IT-outsourcing remote-administration channels, domain controllers and Exchange/mail servers supporting defense and DIB networks [S4][S7][S8]. STEP 2: Trust relationships with service providers bypass perimeter defenses; unpatched Zerologon and Exchange exposure shorten time-to-compromise [S4][S7][S8]. STEP 3: Doctrinal template is spear-phishing or public-facing exploit, then DLL side-loaded RAT (PlugX, ANEL, Hartip), credential theft, lateral movement via MSP access, and staged exfiltration of IP and policy documents [S4][S5][S6][S7][S8]. STEP 4: MLCOA is long-dwell espionage against contractors and allied (especially Japanese) partners through MSP and mail-server access to collect technology and national-security information [S2][S7][S9]. MDCOA is simultaneous compromise of multiple shared service providers to gain persistent access across many DoD-adjacent customers before a crisis [S4][S3]. Candidate indicators: anomalous MSP admin-account logons outside maintenance windows, legitimate binaries (e.g., VLC) loading unsigned DLLs from user paths, Zerologon exploitation events on domain controllers, password-protected macro documents with diplomatic or maritime lures, and VS Code tunnel traffic from servers [S6][S7][S8][S11].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: map which mission systems depend on third-party MSPs and track their compromise reporting, since victims in Cloud Hopper were reached through providers [S4]. (2) Authorities: activity against contractor and MSP networks falls outside DODIN boundaries; coordinate via DC3/DIB CS, FBI and partner-nation agencies (NCSC, NPA) that have attributed this actor [S2][S3][S9]. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize patching and monitoring of domain controllers and Exchange servers, the observed entry points [S7][S8]. (4) Coordination: Japan-focused targeting makes combined information sharing with Japanese partners relevant for INDOPACOM-supporting networks [S7][S9][S11].

provenance.importedSummary: menuPass is a threat group that has been active since at least 2006. Individual members of menuPass are known to have acted in association with the Chinese Ministry of State Security's (MSS) Tianjin State Security Bureau and worked for the Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Company.
